location: Boundaries > Always > Runner ('Exactly one record per admitted cell per run')
issue: The sentence is unconditional, but cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage and Runner > Output say a child that reports `status: skipped` or exits 2 leaves no record. CAP-3 also says 'nothing is appended for the exit-2 version itself'. Today `_SlotRun._on_reaped` returns without records for rc 2 and for a skipped payload. Read literally, the CAP-1 rule requires a record (which one? `crash`? `stopped`?) for those admitted cells, so it contradicts both sources.
implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the spec adds records for exit-2 or skipped children. That breaks CAP-3 tests (child exit 2 leaves nothing for its own version) and the contract. One who follows the contract leaves the spec's invariant untested and the I/O matrix has no row that decides it.
suggestion: Qualify the rule: 'exactly one record per admitted cell per run, except a child that exits 2 or reports skipped, which leaves none (contract Storage)'. Add a test that asserts zero records for those two cases next to the `stopped` tests.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (run's own stop: 'children whose result is already in are reaped normally ... queued cells get no record, as today')
issue: 'Reaped normally' means calling `_on_reaped`. For a reaped `fail` record that calls `_fire('fail-fast after …')`, and for rc 2 it calls `_fire('input-error after …')`. Both append `not-run` records for every still-queued cell, which contradicts 'queued cells get no record'. 'Result already in' is also undefined: a future that is `done()` but not yet popped when JobStopped arrives, a child that has exited but whose future is pending, or an `-o` file that exists. In the current harness (test_e2e_stopped), JobStopped itself comes out of a child future's `result()`, so that child is 'done' and has no result.
implementation_impact: Both readings are plausible: suppress fail-fast in the stop path, or let it write `not-run`. The tests for the Stop row and the queued-cell rule can be written to pass for either reading. When JobStopped interrupts a batch, other done futures in the same batch may be processed or skipped depending on the reading.
suggestion: State the stop path exactly: (1) for every future already `done()` when the stop is handled, other than the one that raised JobStopped, append its records with no fail-fast or exit-2 trigger; (2) every other admitted cell gets `stopped`; (3) queued cells get nothing. Add a test row: stop arrives while a done child holds a `fail` record and one version is still queued, so the `fail` is appended, the queued cell has no record, and the run exits 143.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (`stopped` record contents) vs CAP-3 Design Notes > Records / append error
issue: The spec names only 'build_record fields, claim run_id, tier'. Three points are left open. (a) CAP-3 says a STOPPED_CODES version 'keeps [wait-slots] only in its log'. Should the new `stopped` records merge `wait-slots` into `phase_durations`, as every other record of a spawned version does? (b) After an earlier append error, are `stopped` records still attempted (`force=True`, like reaped child records) or suppressed (like `not-run`/`no-slots`)? (c) For a STOPPED_CODES child that is not the run's own stop, should the `keep` tmp-dir rule apply?
implementation_impact: Each of these is a coin flip, visible in records and tests. (a) changes `phase_durations` shape, which CAP-6 aggregation reads.
suggestion: Add one line: `stopped` records are built like `crash` records (`vres=None`, `wait=wait_res[ver]`, `run_id=claim`, ctx `image_tag`), are appended with `force=True` after an append error, and do not set `keep`. Amend the CAP-3 'keeps it only in its log' note for STOPPED_CODES.

location: Boundaries > Always > Plan (fields) / Docs (hosting version); cell-contract.md > Plan (`e2e_focus_cell`), Phase 1 (hosting version)
issue: The spec pins `e2e_cells_arg = null` for empty next cells, but not `e2e_focus_cell` for `gate`, `done`, `blocked-*` and `blocked-by-scope`. It also does not pin `e2e_warm`/`e2e_scenarios` when a `focus` step is turned into `blocked-by-scope`. The hosting version is defined as 'the version of `e2e_focus_cell` when the orchestrator enters Phase 1 (session start …)', and at session start the plan can already be at `gate` or `done` (canary evidence from an earlier session on the same fingerprint). If `e2e_focus_cell` is null there, the hosting version is undefined. Round-1 implementer-9 raised this, and only `e2e_cells_arg` was fixed.
implementation_impact: A plan that emits `null` (a natural choice for non-tier-0 steps) leaves the docs' hosting rule without a value at session start. A plan that emits the canary is consistent with the contract's literal 'no failing cell → the canary', but tests may assert either.
suggestion: State that `e2e_focus_cell` is always a cell (the focus-cell definition: newest-run failing cell, else the canary) for every step, and that a `focus` step turned into `blocked-by-scope` emits `e2e_warm: false` and `e2e_scenarios: full`. Add both to the Fresh module / Clean module / Scope I/O rows.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs, 4th interim rule ('before an infra retry (re-running a step whose previous run left an infra cause, short of `blocked-infra`)')
issue: The spec does not say how the orchestrator knows that the previous run 'left an infra cause'. The interim read it from the next plan's `rerun_matrix` reasons (`inconclusive`, `inconclusive-steps`, `browser-notes`). Under that test a `stopped` record also reads as `inconclusive`. So after an interactive exit 143 that Budi asks to rerun, the orchestrator would also ask him to 'fix the environment', even though `blocked-infra` explicitly does not treat `stopped` as an infra result. `no-slots` (reason `inconclusive`) is infra; `not-run` is not. It is also unclear whether the prompt applies when the re-derived step differs from the previous one, for example when a gate run's crash cell is retried inside the next `gate` call.
implementation_impact: The docs author must invent the detection rule. Two plausible rules give different prompts after a stop or a fail-fast, and nothing in the tests or ACs can catch the difference.
suggestion: Define it: an infra retry is due when, in the plan after the run, some cell in the run's `appended` list has reason `inconclusive`, `inconclusive-steps` or `browser-notes`, and its newest record's reason is not `stopped`. The cause comes from the run's stderr or progress log. State that `not-run` never triggers the prompt.

location: Boundaries > Always > Docs ('replace the interim orchestration as a whole': Phase 2 loop and wrap-up, `visual-pending.json`); cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 2; tier-matrix.md > Rules / Visual review
issue: The contract says 'spawn the Layer 3 lenses (unless the plan reuses Layer 3)'. `visual-pending` merges 'at Phase 2 start when the plan reuses Layer 3'. But the Phase 2 entry call is `--per-version`, which always lists `adversarial` in `rerun`. The interim explained how to read reuse (a canonical plan call's `layers.adversarial.reuse`) and also kept unmerged lenses spawned under the same fingerprint. That file is being replaced as a whole, and the spec does not say whether these two Layer 3 rules survive. Keeping unmerged same-fingerprint lenses also conflicts with tier-matrix: 'a loop-back … Layer 3 results not yet merged are discarded … lenses spawn again', even when no patch changed the fingerprint.
implementation_impact: The docs writer has no defined way to evaluate 'the plan reuses Layer 3' and must choose between keeping and discarding unmerged lenses after a loop-back. That choice decides whether Layer 3 is respawned, which is costly, and when `visual-pending.json` is merged.
suggestion: Add to the Docs bullet: 'Layer 3 reuse = a canonical plan call (same flags, no `--per-version`) shows `layers.adversarial.reuse` true; on every loop-back, unmerged lens results are discarded whatever their fingerprint (tier-matrix).' Alternatively, emit a `layer3_reuse` field from the plan so the docs read a field instead of making a second call.

location: Design Notes > `clean` ('a per-version file that does not load or fails `validate_layer_shape` = exit 2 naming it, as ps-aggregate does')
issue: (a) ps-aggregate shape-gates only static (with keys `id`/`severity`/`message`) and flashlight. It never gates the scenario payload, so 'as ps-aggregate does' leaves a malformed per-version scenario file, for example `versions` as a list, to crash `scenario_layer` with an AttributeError (traceback, exit 1). (b) `plan_layer` already turns an unreadable file into `rerun` with a reason. If `clean` exits 2 on a file that `plan_layer` judged reusable but malformed, the whole plan call fails. The plan is the only thing that tells the orchestrator which layer to rerun, so the Phase 1 loop has no documented recovery. (c) It is not stated whether the layer files are loaded when `phase1_reuse` is already false for V, in which case `clean` is false anyway.
implementation_impact: There are three implementation choices: validate scenario or not, exit 2 or mark V not clean, load always or only when needed. The choice decides whether a corrupt file stalls Phase 1 or self-heals by rerunning the layer.
suggestion: Specify: load the per-version files only when `per_version[V].phase1_reuse` is true. Shape-gate static (keys), flashlight and scenario (container shape). On failure, either exit 2 naming the file with docs guidance ('rerun that layer for V'), or prefer emitting `clean: false` plus a `clean_reason` naming the file, so the loop reruns it.

issue: Three parts of the generator remain undefined. (a) 'inconclusive (`crash`) cold-full records': real `crash` records from ps-run-layer have `boot`/`scenario_set` null, since no child result is merged, so 'cold-full crash' is a shape the runner never writes. (b) 'stale and warm variants of the cell derived as focus': it is not said whether the variant replaces the focus cell's record or is appended after it, whether the warm record is a pass or a fail, whether partial records are included, or what is generated when the derived focus is the canary with no record. (c) The variants change the derived step, for example a warm pass gives `cold-version`/`cold-canary`, and the AC does not say they are re-derived before the assertion.
implementation_impact: Two implementers write different generators. A weak one, such as appending a warm fail only, never reaches `cold-version`, so the invariant's `cold-version` branch goes untested.
suggestion: Pin the variants: for each combination, derive the focus cell F, then add (i) F's record re-stamped with another fingerprint (stale), (ii) a warm full `pass` appended to F on the current fingerprint, and (iii) a warm `fail` appended to F. Assert the invariant on all four histories. Generate `crash` records with `boot`/`scenario_set` null, as the runner writes them.

location: I/O matrix row 'Promote order' (second case: warm pass then cold full fail)
issue: Under the decided diverge rule (a cold full `fail` on the current fingerprint newer than a warm or partial `pass`), 'warm pass then cold full fail' diverges. The step is `focus` with `e2e_warm: false` and `e2e_scenarios: full`. The row asserts only `focus`, so a test that accepts `e2e_warm: true` there passes.
implementation_impact: The row adds no protection for the diverge rule's second shape (a warm pass that comes before the first cold fail of the fingerprint), which is the case most likely to be implemented wrong when the code scans 'cold fail, then warm pass, then cold fail'.
suggestion: Extend the row's expected output: '/ `focus`, diverges: `e2e_warm` false, `e2e_scenarios` full'.

issue: ps-aggregate's default `--require` is all four layers (plus scenario when shipped). `ready` true therefore also needs static, flashlight and adversarial inputs that pass. The row describes only E2E histories, and does not say whether the test supplies the other layer files or passes `--require e2e`.
implementation_impact: A test with only histories gets `ready: false` and the author 'fixes' it by guessing. With `--require e2e` the row no longer checks the full gate described in the SPEC CAP-1 success criterion.
suggestion: State the fixture: passing static and flashlight files plus an empty-findings adversarial file in `--reports-dir`, default `--require`, `--session` given (so `reached` is true for every version).

location: Tasks > docs / Verification (only AC 3 and a manual check cover docs)
issue: The docs task is the largest change in the slice. It covers the four carried interim rules, hosting version, the Phase 1/2 loops, the Phase 2 entry check, stop convergence, `visual-pending.json`, Headless, the `--tier 0` quickstart and the four callers. Yet the only done criterion is AC 3, checked by hand. Nothing checks that the decided rules (child exit 2 ends the loop; pre-spawn or append exit 2 means fix and rerun, headless `blocked`; exit 143; environment-fix prompt) actually landed, or that the CAP-4/5/7 items stay absent.
implementation_impact: Docs can be partly rewritten and the slice still verifies green. The decided rules from round 1 are exactly what reviewers will look for, and they have no criterion.
suggestion: Add a manual checklist to Verification, one line per rule, each naming the file and section that must state it (run-phases.md 'E2E loop ended', headless.md 'Kembalian', SKILL.md Fase 1/2, the four callers' 'not reached'). Add a grep check that `requires`, `--warm`, `ALIVE idle`, `snapshot-db` and `parallel_only` do not appear in the rewritten sections.

location: Boundaries > Always > Runner (`--tier`) / cell-contract.md > Runner > Input errors (`RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH`)
issue: `--tier` is a ps-run-layer flag, but the spec does not add it to `RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH`. A `--tier 0` placed after `--` therefore passes the pre-spawn checks only if a top-level `--tier` is also given, and then reaches `ps-e2e-run.py`, whose argparse rejects it with exit 2. Under the decided rule, a child exit 2 ends the E2E loop for the whole session. Under the old wording a missing top-level `--tier` is a pre-spawn exit 2, so only the duplicated form reaches the child.
implementation_impact: A one-token mistake in an orchestrator command ends E2E for the session instead of producing a fixable pre-spawn error.
suggestion: Add `--tier` to `RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH` (prefix abbreviations included, as CAP-3 did), and add `--tier` in passthrough to the Bad input row.

location: Boundaries > Always > Aggregate ('`reached` … emitted only when `--session` is given') / Docs
issue: The spec says when the field exists, but not which callers pass `--session` to ps-aggregate. The interim wrap-up and quickstart call the aggregate without `--session`. Headless needs it for `not reached`. Whether the interactive wrap-up and the stop-convergence report should pass it is not stated.
implementation_impact: The docs writer decides alone. If interactive omits `--session`, the interactive report cannot say which versions were not reached after stop convergence or an ended E2E loop, while headless can.
suggestion: State in the Docs bullet: the wrap-up aggregate (interactive and headless) always gets `--session <t>`; the quickstart TDD verdict does not.
